course: Middle-school physical science, grade 6: sound and waves, floating and sinking, heat and circuits
curriculum: Sound is a wave, and it travels through water as well as air
An echo gives a distance, once you know the speed and the time
Loud and quiet, high and low: what a sound tells you about its source
Listening from two places to find where a sound came from
Hearing something quiet next to something loud
Density: why one thing floats and another sinks
Adding weight changes what floats, and how fast it changes
Heat moves from hot to cold, and it needs a path
Circuits: a break, a short, and why water and electricity are dangerous
Air is a mixture, and the share of each gas matters
A rate: how fast something builds up or drains away
Reading a gauge, and taking a measurement more than once
Change one thing at a time, and watch what follows
Deciding under pressure: what can be undone, and what cannot
Two instruments that share a source are really one instrument

groups.name: Sonar & Acoustics

groups.name: Navigation & Position
groups.desc: Where the boat is, how old that answer is, and how wrong it is allowed to be.

groups.name: Damage Control
groups.desc: Water in the boat — finding it, stopping it, and knowing whether you are winning.

groups.name: Fire & Electrical
groups.desc: Fire aboard is an electrical problem until the power is proved gone.

groups.name: Atmosphere & Life Support
groups.desc: The air is a system with sources, sinks and a flow path, and people are in it.

groups.name: Propulsion & Engineering
groups.desc: What turns the shaft, what cools it, and what the boat gives away by running it.
